title.rendered: 2019: Governorship Aspirant Solicits Imo Stakeholders’ Support

content.rendered:
Chief Obioma Success Akagburuonye, a governorship aspirant in Imo State on the platform of National Unity Party (NUP) at the weekend sought the support of the apex body of the state’s stakeholders under the auspices of Imo Zuru Kwuo, for the actualisation of his ambition.

Akagburuonye, who spoke to the stakeholders made up of the group’s governing council members, local government coordinators, religious leaders, party chieftains, professionals, market and civil society organisations, restated his desire to run the race to victory.

The Abuja-based businessman and legal practitioner said his request for the stakeholders’ support followed the decision of Imo people to liberate and restore hope in the state come 2019.

He said his humble background, hard work and integrity had placed him in a vantage financial position for governance, even as he pledged an all-inclusive and non-discriminatory administration if elected into power.

He also promised to focus on infrastructure, job creation and empowerment as well as improvement of the state’s Internally Generated Revenue (IGR).

Bright Olaokpu, NUP state chairman, who accompanied the aspirant to the meeting, described his party as a repositioned grassroots platform to drive Imo restoration, stressing that integrated and simultaneous access and infrastructure developments, industrialisation, job creation and a revised education system would form the basis of the party’s programmes in the state.

Dr Darlington Akukwu, the chairman, Governing Council of Imo Zuru Kwuo, welcomed the aspirant, stressing that the body had been saddled with the task of building the path of enthronement of humane and purposeful governance for Imo State come 2019.

Akukwu, the state chapter chairman of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), assured Akagburuonye of a level playing ground, even as he challenged him and the others on a clear manifesto bordering on revamping the state’s economy in relation to its current huge debt status.

He urged the aspirant to focus on healthcare, education, infrastructure development, insecurity as well as the people’s welfare.

Chief Uche Njoku, the President General of Imo Zuru Kwuo, traced the group’s mission to the need to liberating the state from unholy and unrighteous government, even as he expressed delight at the caliber of aspirants that had so far emerged.
